## Real acceptance criteria (from Jira SFCC-91's structured "Acceptance Criteria" custom field, current version — NOT the PR description's paraphrase, which you should treat as a secondary source only)

*Swatch availability*
- Given a product has only one colour, when the PDP loads, then the colour is displayed as a text label (e.g. "Colour: Bay Blue") and no swatches are rendered.
- Given a product has multiple colour variations, when the PDP loads, then the index image for each colour variation is displayed as a swatch.
- Given multiple colour swatches are displayed, when the PDP loads, then the currently viewed colour variation's swatch is visually indicated as selected.

*Swatch selection*
- Given a shopper clicks a colour swatch, when the selection is registered, then the URL updates to reflect the selected colour variation without full page reload.
(Note: an earlier "New Style Code... URL updates... with a new style code and a full page reload" AC existed but was deliberately REMOVED from this ticket on 2026-08-12 and deferred to SFCC-708 — so the PR correctly does NOT implement a full-reload/new-style-code behaviour. Do not flag its absence.)

*Index image not populated*
- Given a colour variation exists but has not been enabled, when the PDP loads, then that colour variation's swatch is not rendered and the variation is not surfaced to the shopper.

*Pagination* (not a formal Jira AC — sourced from a real Figma interaction annotation on node 40003328:115594 in file wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm, which I fetched directly via the Figma MCP myself): "Pagination appears if there are more than 4 swatches. If chevron is clicked, the next set of swatches appears. If Label/Colour name is longer, use truncation."

  - `npx tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors on both head and base.

All 16 warnings are pre-existing (same warnings, shifted line numbers). This is a real, confirmed, in-scope defect — the PR fails `npm run lint` due to its own new files. I already have this finding; you don't need to re-derive it, but feel free to independently confirm if useful.
  - `npm run test` (vitest): BASE = 408/408 passed (26 files). HEAD = 433/433 passed (28 files). No failures, no regressions.
- **Figma design fidelity — I fetched the live nodes directly (file `wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm`, "Zimmermann_Design_System_2026") and cross-checked against the actual token values in `theme/foundation/colour.ts`/`spacing.ts`. All confirmed exact matches, not approximate:**

  - Selected state = `border-b` (bottom-only) in Figma, colour `#191919` = `grey[900]` = the codebase's `--zimm-color-border-focus` exactly. The PR's bottom-only border and its `borderBottomColor: var(--zimm-color-border-focus)` are correct.
  - Background on all 3 states = Figma `#f6f4f1` = `ivory[200]` = codebase's `--zimm-color-bg-02` exactly. Correct.
  - Focus ring: Figma's ring is `1px` (= codebase's `borderWidths.default`) at offsets top:-2px/right:-2.13px/bottom:-3px/left:-2px (i.e. ~2px on 3 of 4 sides, 3px on the bottom) — codebase's `focusRingOffsets.default` is a flat `2px`, matching 3 of 4 sides exactly, ~1px off on the bottom. The PR's code comment calls this "export noise" rather than a deliberate asymmetric design and mirrors `zimmNavItem.css.ts`'s existing uniform-outline pattern instead of replicating the asymmetry. I consider this a reasonable, defensible engineering judgment call given how small the discrepancy is and that there's no other precedent for a non-uniform ring anywhere in this codebase — not a fidelity defect. Don't re-litigate this one unless you find something I didn't (e.g. if the *colour* of the ring were wrong, that would be new — but I checked, it's the same `#191919`/`grey[900]` via `--zimm-color-border-focus`/`--zimm-focus-ring`, correct).
  - `textStyle="caption"` for the "Colour: Bay Blue" label — Figma specs a "Caption-strong" style (12px/500-weight/18px-lineheight/0 letterspacing). I checked `typography.ts`: the codebase's single registered `caption` textStyle already resolves to exactly fontSize 12px / fontWeight 500 (medium) / lineHeight 18px / letterSpacing 0 — an exact match despite the naming difference. Not a bug.
  - Pagination row layout (label left, chevrons right, same row) matches Figma's `labelContainer` structure exactly.
  - `--zimm-color-icon-disabled` token (new, Tier 1) — sourced from the real Figma chevron nodes (40003328:115592–115595), confirmed by me.
  - **Do not spend budget re-verifying any of the above token/geometry/colour matches.** I already pulled the live Figma nodes and diffed them against the actual foundation files myself.

`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts`, the `pageButton._disabled` block (around line 159-168): the comment immediately above the `_disabled` object says "No confirmed Figma spec for a disabled visual treatment on this control... only the cursor affordance is set here, which is a UX keyword, not a design token" — but the `_disabled` object right below it sets BOTH `cursor: 'not-allowed'` AND `color: 'var(--zimm-color-icon-disabled)'`. The color line IS a real visual treatment via a real design token, directly contradicting what the comment right above it claims. This looks like a stale comment left over from before the "post-build fixes" commit (0aff491) added the disabled-colour styling, never updated afterward. Confirm this reading is right, and assess how it should be characterized (comment accuracy / maintainability issue — the code itself is very likely correct, since the disabled-icon token was separately confirmed sourced from real Figma nodes; it's the comment that's now false).

## What to actually spend your budget on

1. **Correctness/regression** — `product-view/index.tsx`'s new render-slot: verify the `??`-based fallback logic is actually correct (there's a whole commit, 2d8a9a7, fixing a self-contradictory JSDoc about this — read the final code, not just the doc, and confirm the described null-vs-undefined behaviour is what the code actually does). Check `product-detail/index.tsx`'s wiring: does it correctly resolve `disBaseLink || link` per variation, correctly restrict to `id === 'color'` only, and correctly leave set/bundle child `ProductView` instances on base rendering (the PR claims this is untouched — verify).
2. **Conventions/tier ownership** — confirm no protected path outside what's disclosed (Tier 1: `theme/foundation/{colour,zimmTokens}.ts`; Tier 2: `theme/components/index.ts`) was touched; confirm `.claude/registry/*.md` changes look like genuine regenerated output, not hand-edits (check for `generateRegistry.mjs` still being the stated source per the CodeRabbit thread); confirm naming/file-layout conventions per `.claude/rules/components.md` and `conventions.md`.

4. **Test coverage quality** — per `.claude/rules/testing.md`, do the two new test files actually assert behaviour (not implementation details)? Is there a test gap for `product-view/index.tsx`'s new render-slot itself (I don't see a dedicated `product-view` test file in either base or head's vitest output — confirm whether one exists or should)?
5. **Failure modes/security** — any place a missing/malformed value could throw or leak unsanitized data (e.g. `imageUrl` interpolated into a CSS `background-image: url(...)`, `name` used as `aria-label` — SFCC-controlled data, but worth a quick look for XSS/CSS-injection surface).
6. **DRY/duplication** — spot-check `SWATCHES_PER_PAGE` sharing and i18n message id reuse claims in the commit messages actually hold in the final code.

Report findings with file:line, a one-sentence summary, and a concrete failure scenario for each — the format `ReportFindings` expects. Don't report on anything in the "already verified" list above as if it were new.

8	// `Link` is what actually delivers "URL updates without a full page reload": it pushes history
9	// rather than navigating the document. There is no overrides/.../link equivalent to reuse
10	// instead — confirmed none exists for this.
11	const ColourSwatchLink = chakra(RouteLink);

13	type ZimmColourSwatchProps = {
14	  /** Colour display name. Not rendered as visible text — used as the accessible name (`aria-label`). */
15	  name: string;
16	  /**
17	   * Fully resolved image URL for this colour's swatch fill. Resolution is the caller's job —
18	   * this component performs no SFCC-shape lookup of its own.
19	   */
20	  imageUrl: string;
21	  /**
22	   * Destination URL for this colour variation. Absent for the quick-view-modal path, where
23	   * SFCC's own `useVariationAttributes` returns `href: null` and the swatch must not navigate.
24	   */
25	  href?: string;
26	  /** Whether this is the currently selected colour. */
27	  isSelected: boolean;
28	  /**
29	   * Whether this swatch is reachable via Tab (`tabIndex={0}`) vs. removed from the tab order
30	   * (`tabIndex={-1}`) — the caller drives a roving tabindex across the swatch group.
31	   */
32	  isFocusable: boolean;
33	};

35	/**
36	 * Atom — a single colour swatch in a PDP colour-variation list: a clickable rectangle filled
37	 * with that colour's product photo, radio semantics (one selection out of the group), and a
38	 * router `Link` when a destination URL exists so selecting a colour updates the URL without a
39	 * full page reload.
40	 *
41	 * Purely presentational — no data-fetching hook of any kind. SFCC data resolution (building
42	 * `imageUrl`/`href` from a product's variation attributes) happens at the page level, not this
43	 * atom.
44	 */
45	export const ZimmColourSwatch = ({ name, imageUrl, href, isSelected, isFocusable }: ZimmColourSwatchProps) => {
46	  // Above any early return — there isn't one here, this component always renders something.
47	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_COLOUR_SWATCH_RECIPE, { selected: isSelected });
48	
49	  // The dynamic URL genuinely cannot live in the static recipe file, so this one dynamic `__css`
50	  // spread is the correct, deliberate exception — the same shape already used at
51	  // footer/footerNavColumn/index.tsx:44 and :62, an established pattern in this codebase.
52	  const image = <chakra.span __css={{ ...styles.image, backgroundImage: `url(${imageUrl})` }} />;
53	
54	  /*
55	   * Deliberately no `backgroundColor={name.toLowerCase()}` here, unlike base SFCC's own
56	   * `renderDefaultVariationAttribute` (product-view/index.jsx, and our own extraction of it in
57	   * product-view/index.tsx). Three reasons this stays out, permanently, not an oversight to
58	   * "fix" back in later:
59	   *   1. It uses the colour's display name as a raw CSS colour keyword — "Ivory" resolves as a
60	   *      real CSS colour, "Bay Blue" does not — which is both unauditable by `audit:tokens` and
61	   *      against this codebase's no-raw-design-value rule.
62	   *   2. In base it exists to tint the swatch behind a *missing* product image. This component is
63	   *      only ever rendered for colour variations that already have a populated image — the
64	   *      caller filters out any variation without one before rendering this component at all —
65	   *      so there is never a missing image for a fallback tint to show behind.
66	   *   3. Even if one slipped through, `background-size: cover` on the image (see the recipe's
67	   *      `image` part) would hide any tint sitting behind it regardless.
68	   */

71	      <ColourSwatchLink
72	        to={href}
73	        __css={styles.swatch}
74	        role="radio"
75	        aria-checked={isSelected}
76	        aria-label={name}
77	        tabIndex={isFocusable ? 0 : -1}
78	        data-testid="colour-swatch"

81	      </ColourSwatchLink>

{"body":"# Description Implements PDP colour swatches and variation selection (SFCC-91). A `renderVariationAttribute` render slot is added to the `product-view` override, and two new `ui-kits` components — `ZimmColourSwatch` (atom) and `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` (molecule) — are wired into the PDP via that slot for the `color` attribute. Delivers: - **AC 1** — single populated colour renders as a text label only (no swatches) - **AC 2** — each populated colour renders as a swatch image at 48×72 (2/3 aspect ratio) - **AC 3** — selected colour is indicated by a bottom border in `--zimm-color-border-focus` - **AC 4** — selecting a colour updates the URL without a full page reload (RouteLink) - **AC 5** — colours with no index image are filtered out; unpopulated slots are not rendered - **Pagination** — >4 colours paginate with left/right chevrons; disabled chevron dims to `--zimm-color-icon-disabled` when at the first/last page Adds `--zimm-color-icon-disabled` (`grey[200]` / `#D1D1D1`) as a new token to the icon alias tier in `colour.ts` / `zimmTokens.ts` — Tier 1 edit, authorised by Marcel Navarro (repo admin) per the Figma spec (`--alias-color-icon-disabled`).
